authors: Angelopoulos, A. N.; Bates, S.
venue: Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 16(4), 494-591
problem: Tutorial on conformal prediction
method: Split conformal; CQR; conditional-coverage diagnostics; extensions
environment_or_data: Tutorial examples
key_results: Distribution-free, finite-sample marginal coverage with any pre-trained model; stresses that conformal guarantees are marginal, conditional coverage is impossible in general
limitations: Tutorial (no new results)
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.07511 (abstract + Sec. 1, conditional-coverage paragraph); Crossref abstract

authors: Bingqing Chen; Priya L. Donti; Kyri Baker; J. Zico Kolter; M. Berges
venue: Proc. 12th ACM Int. Conf. Future Energy Systems (e-Energy '21)
problem: RL policies for energy systems whose actions must satisfy convex operational constraints (building HVAC, inverter voltage control).
method: PROF: differentiable projection layer onto an approximate convex constraint set (Euclidean projection, Eq. 7) inside the policy; gradients via implicit differentiation of KKT conditions (Sec. 3.2, Eqs. 8-9); auxiliary loss lambda*||pi - pi_hat||^2 between pre- and post-projection actions (Eq. 16).
architecture: Building: LSTM Gaussian policy trained with PPO; inverters: utility-level + per-inverter networks trained by differentiating through a linearised grid model
environment_or_data: EnergyPlus 600 m2 building (Pittsburgh weather); IEEE 37-bus feeder with 21 PV inverters, 1-s steps over a week
baselines: Building: P-controller, Gnu-RL, Agent #6, 'LSTM & Clip' ablations; inverters: IEEE 1547.8 Volt/Var, optimum of linearised model, AC-OPF optimum
key_results: Heating demand 33,271 vs 34,687 kW (about 4% saving vs Gnu-RL); Volt/Var violates voltage limits 22.3% of the time vs 0% for PROF; projection 8.6 ms vs network 4.5 ms (Sec. 5.3, 6.3, 7).
limitations: Feasibility only w.r.t. an approximate (linearised) constraint set; building comfort violated when control saturates; per-step solver cost; no scaling study in number of devices.
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.08881 (arXiv version of the e-Energy paper)

authors: Niangjun Chen; Christian Kurniawan; Yorie Nakahira; Lijun Chen; Steven H. Low
problem: Online adaptive EV charging as feasibility problem (energy by deadline, rate limits, station power limit)
method: Smoothed least-laxity-first (sLLF): maximise concave sum of next-slot laxities; closed-form clipped water-filling with common level found by bisection
environment_or_data: ACN Caltech CAGarage, Google Mountain View and Sunnyvale traces (52,362 sessions, 104 locations)
baselines: EDF, LLF, equal share, remaining-energy-proportional, online LP; offline LP for min feasible power
key_results: Rate r_i = clip(rbar_i(L - laxity_i + 1), 0, min(rbar_i, e_i)); 100% feasibility with only 7% power augmentation (EDF 139%, OLP 28%); theorems on power(+rate) augmentation
limitations: Online feasibility not guaranteed without augmentation; known departure and energy assumed; no prices/profit objective

authors: Gal Dalal; Krishnamurthy Dvijotham; Matej Vecerik; Todd Hester; Cosmin Paduraru; Yuval Tassa
problem: Never violating hard state constraints while an RL agent learns on a physical system (e.g., data-centre cooling, robots).
method: Safety layer added to the policy that analytically solves a per-state action-correction problem; closed form obtained via a linearised constraint model learned from logged data.
environment_or_data: New physics-based environments
key_results: Zero constraint violations reported where reward shaping fails (abstract).
limitations: Safety relies on an approximate learned linear model; the closed form is commonly noted to assume a single active constraint at a time (as summarised by su2025review).

authors: Sebastien Gros; Mario Zanon; Alberto Bemporad
problem: Whether projecting RL actions onto a safe set disrupts learning and optimality.
method: Analysis for Q-learning (projection of greedy policy is generally suboptimal; fix: constrained minimisation of Q with restricted TD targets, Lemma 1) and for policy gradients: deterministic case uses the projected-policy Jacobian M(x) (null-space projector of active constraints, Prop. 1/Cor. 1); stochastic case uses the score of the unprojected sample with the advantage of the projected action (Prop. 2); extension to robust-MPC projections (Cor. 2-3).
environment_or_data: Linear system with circular state constraint; robust linear MPC as projection (Sec. 6)
key_results: Unbiased policy-gradient corrections under LICQ/SOSC; qualitative convergence plots only.
limitations: Assumes LICQ and strict SOSC; stochastic result is asymptotic (barrier parameter -> 0); single small example.

authors: Hu, S.; Zhu, F.; Chang, X.; Liang, X.
problem: Multi-agent RL across tasks with different numbers of agents/entities
method: MARL (plugged into value-based MARL pipelines)
architecture: UPDeT: transformer over observation entities; policy decoupling maps attention outputs to entity-related actions
environment_or_data: StarCraft multi-agent tasks of different sizes (e.g. 3v3, 5v6 per abstract)
key_results: One architecture handles different observation/action configurations and transfers across tasks (abstract-level)
limitations: Game domain; no physical constraints

authors: Jin, B.; Sun, S.; Zhang, Y.; Zheng, S.; Yu, H.
problem: Zero-shot active voltage control across distribution feeders under imperfect telemetry
method: TD3-style graph actor-critic (GRAS-AVC) with imitation and risk terms
architecture: Permutation-equivariant shared actor: 3 edge-conditioned message-passing layers, shared per-inverter head, droop prior + residual; variable-size twin graph critics (mean/max pooling)
environment_or_data: 7 source feeders (15-141 buses) for training; zero-shot 322-bus target (38 DERs)
baselines: Droop, matched Graph-TD3 (with/without selector), feeder-specific MATD3
key_results: Same weights 15-141 buses -> 322 buses (6->38 DERs); violating bus-time 7.455% (droop) -> 2.723% with runtime AC power-flow screening
limitations: One-step screening not a multi-step certificate; one target feeder; 5 seeds; requires physical model at deployment

authors: Krzysztof C. Kiwiel
problem: Continuous quadratic knapsack problem (separable quadratic objective, one linear equality, box bounds) - the problem class of Euclidean projection onto a box intersected with a hyperplane.
method: Several linear-time breakpoint-searching algorithms; identifies cycling and wrong-convergence examples in existing algorithms.
environment_or_data: Large-scale computational tests
key_results: Linear-time algorithms with encouraging large-scale results (abstract).
limitations: Abstract only; problem formulation details to be checked against full text before quoting specifics.

authors: Christos D. Korkas; Christos D. Tsaknakis; Athanasios Ch. Kapoutsis; Elias Kosmatopoulos
problem: Station with N charging spots, PV and V2G: cost minimisation and user satisfaction
method: Distributed MARL: one DDPG agent per charging spot trained with difference rewards from a coordinator
architecture: Per-spot MLP DDPG actor/critic with fixed 10-value local observation
environment_or_data: Chargym environment; four price profiles incl. NordPool; typical PV day; 10/20/35/50 spots
baselines: Rule-based controllers; centralised DDPG and SAC
key_results: Up to 25% energy-cost reduction and up to 20% user-satisfaction improvement (abstract); local observation size constant across station sizes
limitations: Departure SoC only penalised; no aggregate transformer cap in model; weight sharing/transfer across sizes not stated
evidence_source: https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/17/15/3694 (HTML, partial; results section not reached)

authors: Lee, J.; Lee, Y.; Kim, J.; Kosiorek, A. R.; Choi, S.; Teh, Y. W.
problem: Learning on set-structured inputs
method: Supervised learning
architecture: Set Transformer: attention-based permutation-invariant encoder/decoder; inducing-point attention reduces cost from quadratic to linear in set size
environment_or_data: Multiple-instance learning, 3D shape recognition, few-shot classification
key_results: Attention captures interactions among set elements; inducing points give linear-time attention (abstract-level)
limitations: Not RL; no constraints

authors: Lei, J.; G'Sell, M.; Rinaldo, A.; Tibshirani, R. J.; Wasserman, L.
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association 113(523)
problem: Distribution-free predictive inference for regression
method: Full and split conformal prediction; jackknife; in-sample split conformal
environment_or_data: Simulations and real data (high-dimensional regression)
key_results: Split conformal (Alg. 2): residual quantile k=ceil((n/2+1)(1-alpha)) on held-out half; Thm 2.2: coverage >= 1-alpha under i.i.d., and <= 1-alpha+2/(n+2) if residuals continuous
limitations: Marginal (not conditional) coverage; needs i.i.d./exchangeable data

authors: Hannah Markgraf; Shambhuraj Sawant; Hanna Krasowski; Lukas Schaefer; Sebastien Gros; Matthias Althoff
problem: Whether a projection safeguard should be part of the environment (SE-RL) or of the policy as a differentiable layer (SP-RL).
method: Unified actor-critic formalisation of SE-RL and SP-RL; Theorem 1 (optimal value functions coincide), Lemma 1 (equivalence for stochastic policies with GAE), Lemma 2 (action aliasing: actions in the normal cone map to the same safe action -> rank-deficient Jacobian), Lemma 3 (flat-lining critic in SE-RL); mitigation via reward penalty (SE-RL), per-sample loss and a new penalty critic (PenC) for SP-RL (Sec. 5-7).
environment_or_data: Pendulum and quadrotor stabilisation (RCI sets), seeker navigation (state-dependent safe set), building energy-management task
baselines: Vanilla vs improved SE-RL and SP-RL variants
key_results: A2C: SE-RL = SP-RL; TD3: vanilla SE-RL often beats vanilla SP-RL, improved SP-RL matches or beats penalised SE-RL; improved SP-RL costs about 3-12x SE-RL compute (Sec. 8-9).
limitations: Preprint; PPO/SAC not analysed; safety by construction of the projection onto given safe sets (theorems concern learning, not safety).

authors: Orfanoudakis S.; Diaz-Londono C.; Yilmaz Y.E.; Palensky P.; Vergara P.P.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems 26(2):2410-2421 (online Dec 2024)
problem: Open Gym simulator for EV smart charging/V2G at CPO level (chargers grouped under transformers); case studies PST (20 chargers) and V2G profit max with loads (10 bidirectional chargers)
method: Simulator + benchmark of RL (SB3: A2C, ARS, SAC, DDPG, TD3, TQC, PPO, TRPO), heuristics, MPC and Gurobi oracle
architecture: n/a (environment); flat Box action of size = number of EVSE ports, per-port in [0,1] (G2V) or [-1,1] (V2G) scaled to charger max current; flat observation whose length grows with #ports
constraint_handling: other:env clips EVSE/BMS current; transformer overload NOT blocked (only measured) + penalty in reward
environment_or_data: EV2Gym; ElaadNL arrivals/departures/energy, Pecan Street loads, Renewables.ninja PV, ENTSO-E prices; 15-min steps (configurable), ~85-112 steps/episode
baselines: AFAP, ALAP, Round Robin; real-time MPC (eMPC/OCMF in code); Gurobi optimal (perfect information)
key_results: PST 20 chargers (100 runs): energy-tracking error Optimal 46+-14 kWh, RR 57+-16, AFAP 313+-59, RL 213-295 kWh; V2G 10 chargers: TD3 profit 31.1 EUR but user satisfaction 38%, Optimal 100% satisfaction
limitations: Fixed-size flat state/action; RL baselines reach very low user satisfaction; no power flow in paper version; departure energy hard only in MIP (in code v2.0.0 the Gurobi profit-max oracle uses a quadratic satisfaction penalty and hard transformer limit)
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.01849 (WebFetch) + EV2Gym 2.0.0 source from PyPI (MIT license)

authors: Orfanoudakis S.; Robu V.; Salazar E.M.; Palensky P.; Vergara P.P.
problem: CPO-level PST (and V2G profit) over 25/100/500/1000 charge points grouped by transformers
method: EV-GNN: end-to-end GNN actor/critic combined with SAC/TD3 (also multi-discrete TD3); branch pruning of empty chargers
architecture: Heterogeneous graph (EV, charger, transformer, CPO nodes), type-specific MLP encoders + GCN layers; per-node action output; critic with mean pooling
environment_or_data: EV2Gym; ElaadNL, RVO, ENTSO-E
baselines: AFAP, Round Robin, MPC/oracle (Gurobi), A2C, DDPG, TRPO, TQC, SAC, TD3, PPO variants, FX-GNN
key_results: 1000 CPs: SAC EV-GNN 98.7% user satisfaction, 11 MWh tracking error vs classic SAC 95.9%/17 MWh; actor ~256k vs ~2.8M parameters
limitations: Separate model trained per scale (no train-small/test-large zero-shot in preprint); no transformer/departure constraint enforcement; authors list safe RL as future work; 'prove' in abstract is empirical
evidence_source: Research Square preprint rs-5504138 v1 PDF (WebFetch); published abstract via OpenAlex

authors: Stavros Orfanoudakis; Bob Elders; Peter Palensky; Pedro P. Vergara
venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science (ECML PKDD 2025 workshops), vol. 2841
problem: Large-scale EV dispatch / charging coordination
method: End-to-end TD3 enhanced with graph neural networks plus a safety layer
environment_or_data: Real EV charging sessions
key_results: Abstract: safety layer intended to ensure grid stability, preserve EV charging requirements and enforce power limits; coordinates large fleets (no numbers in abstract)
limitations: Abstract only; whether the safety layer is provable, whether departure energy is guaranteed, and whether zero-shot size transfer is tested are UNKNOWN; full text paywalled. HIGHEST-PRIORITY NOVELTY CHECK

authors: Orfanoudakis S.; Panda N.K.; Palensky P.; Vergara P.P.
problem: CPO V2G smart charging (25 chargers main; 250 chargers scaled) with aggregate power limit and departure energy targets
method: GNN-DT: offline Decision Transformer conditioned on return-to-go, trained on random/round-robin/optimal trajectories
architecture: GCN state/action embedders + GPT-2 causal transformer (3 layers, 4 heads); per-node action by dot product of output token with node embedding; masking of absent EVs
environment_or_data: EV2Gym, 15-min steps, 300-step (3-day) episodes
baselines: DT, Q-DT, SAC, DDPG, TD3, TRPO, PPO, TQC, BaU round robin, CAFAP, offline optimal
key_results: 25 chargers: user satisfaction 99.3%, power violation 21.7+-22.8 (optimal 2.0+-4.6, BaU 10.5); journal abstract: rewards within 5% of oracle; zero-shot 25->5/50/75/100 chargers degrades with size but stays above BaU
limitations: Imitation of offline data; constraints only through reward/data quality; violations higher than BaU; zero-shot only up to 100 chargers; 250-charger case retrained
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.01778 (arXiv preprint, WebFetch); journal abstract via OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar

authors: Phipps, K.; Schwenk, K.; Briegel, B.; Mikut, R.; Hagenmeyer, V.
problem: Uncertainty of parking-duration predictions for user-centric smart charging
method: Split prediction errors into critical (undercharging) and non-critical parts; quantile-based security levels from probabilistic forecasts matched to user risk preference
environment_or_data: Semi-synthetic open mobility dataset; real EV trip data
key_results: Customised UQ can regulate critical (undercharging) errors on real data (abstract-level)
limitations: Abstract does not mention conformal calibration or finite-sample guarantee; not embedded in a controller (abstract-level)

authors: Romano, Y.; Patterson, E.; Candes, E. J.
problem: Adaptive distribution-free prediction intervals
method: Conformalized quantile regression (CQR): fit lower/upper quantile regressors, conformalize with score max(q_lo-Y, Y-q_hi)
environment_or_data: 11 regression benchmark datasets
baselines: Split conformal, locally adaptive conformal, uncalibrated quantile regression
key_results: Thm 1: P(Y in C(X)) >= 1-alpha under exchangeability; quantile of scores at (1-alpha)(1+1/|I2|); Thm 2 asymmetric two-tailed version; uncalibrated quantile NNs can under-cover
limitations: Marginal coverage only; quantile crossing possible

authors: Nasrin Sadeghianpourhamami; Johannes Deleu; Chris Develder
problem: Joint coordination of a set of EV charging stations for load flattening (demand response)
method: Batch RL: fitted Q-iteration on a new MDP whose state bins EVs by time-to-departure and remaining charging time
architecture: MLP Q-function (128-64 ReLU) over a binned 2-D grid state independent of number of stations; fractional action per bin
environment_or_data: ElaadNL public charging transactions (busiest 10 and 50 stations, 2015)
key_results: Cost reduction vs BAU 39% (10 stations) and 30.4% (50 stations); learned policy 13% / 15.6% above oracle cost; policy trained on 10 stations tested with up to 10x scaled arrivals (largest jump at 2x)
limitations: Unfinished-charging only penalised (large M), no violation statistics; no transformer limit; same charging rate assumed for all EVs; discrete binning
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1809.10679v2 (arXiv version of the TSG paper)

authors: Wang X.; Nimalsiri N.I.; Xia Y.; Wang P.; Halgamuge S.K.
problem: Voltage-safe EV charging in nested CRE21 Australian distribution networks: 1-32 transformers, 200-3,218 EVs (one charger per EV), hourly decisions
method: Parameter-shared heterogeneous-graph SAC with PID-Lagrangian voltage cost + safety filter (learned graph residual risk sets intervention authority, LinDistFlow projection via truncated POCS sets direction)
architecture: Heterogeneous bus/EV graph, edge-aware message passing with GraphGPS-style global token and EV cross-attention; 383,702 parameters at all scales
environment_or_data: pandapower AC power flow; Ausgrid demand/PV, AEMO prices, VISTA mobility; 240 train / 100 eval days
baselines: ISAC, centralized SAC, MADDPG, perfect-information LP (PI-LP); filter ablations
key_results: Bus-step voltage violations 3.93-7.74% (no filter) -> 0.52-3.44%; departure success 99.06-100%; zero-shot 8->16/32 transformers (2,239/3,218 EVs): 0.57-0.75% violations, >=99.99% departure success
limitations: Explicitly no pointwise feasibility claim; Proposition 1 only gives sign of LinDistFlow correction; departure energy via reward + heuristic service map; transformer loading not constrained

authors: Haoyu Yan; Shutong Ding; Jiebao Zhang; Xi Yao; Yu Liu; Haoyu Wang; Chenchi Luo; Ye Shi
problem: Spatio-temporal V2G scheduling inside optimal power flow with coupled grid and EV-energy constraints.
method: HPC-RL: upper level GRG-SAC (generalised-reduced-gradient embedding, Newton completion of non-basic variables, projection of violating inequalities; Prop. 4.1 first-order feasibility); lower level 'dynamic boundary' per-EV power bounds from remaining energy and remaining intervals (Sec. 4.1-4.2, Eq. 16).
architecture: SAC with GRG layer + rule-based per-EV allocation
environment_or_data: IEEE 14-, 30- and modified 141-bus systems; 10 EVs connected per time step
baselines: MPC, penalty-based RL, optimisation-embedded RL, projection-based RL, CRL
key_results: Abstract: near-zero violation rate, nearly 100% demand satisfied, online computation reduced from hours to minutes; moderate cost gap to MPC.
limitations: Departure-energy guarantee asserted without theorem in the text we read; grid feasibility only to Newton tolerance and requires nonsingular Jacobian block; fleet size not varied; result tables not reached in our reading.

authors: Ye, Z.; Gao, Y.; Yu, N.
problem: Profit-maximising operation of an EV charging station with V2G
method: CADE: centralised allocation + decentralised execution; DQN
architecture: One DQN (256-128-64) shared by all homogeneous chargers with a shared replay memory; per-charger state incl. station-level summary features
constraint_handling: penalty+other:feasible discrete action set per charger
environment_or_data: Synthetic Poisson arrivals for office/residential/highway/retail sites
baselines: MPC (1 h/2 h), MPC-ideal, greedy urgency heuristic (with/without V2G)
key_results: Beats all baselines except MPC-ideal; sizes 10-100 chargers evaluated with per-step compute 0.7-1.7 ms vs MPC 3-935 s; text does not clearly state whether one trained model was reused across sizes
limitations: Departure energy via shortfall penalty; station peak only via demand charge; synthetic data; homogeneous chargers

authors: Joshua Achiam; David Held; Aviv Tamar; Pieter Abbeel
problem: Policy search for RL with safety constraints expressed as expected cumulative costs.
method: Constrained Policy Optimization (CPO): trust-region policy update with a constraint on the expected cost; relies on a new bound relating the returns of two policies to their average divergence.
environment_or_data: Simulated robot locomotion tasks with safety-motivated constraints
key_results: Qualitative: near-constraint satisfaction at each policy iteration, guarantees on policy behaviour throughout training (per abstract).
limitations: Guarantee concerns expected cost and is approximate ('near-constraint satisfaction'); no per-step/per-state feasibility.

authors: Agarwal, R.; Schwarzer, M.; Castro, P. S.; Courville, A.; Bellemare, M. G.
problem: Reliable evaluation of deep RL with few runs
method: Interval estimates via stratified bootstrap CIs; performance profiles; interquartile mean (IQM)
environment_or_data: Atari 100k and other benchmarks
key_results: Point estimates with few runs are unreliable; IQM has much smaller CIs than median (Fig. 2/Sec. 4); recommends stratified bootstrap CIs
limitations: Focus on multi-task benchmarks

authors: Akshay Agrawal; Brandon Amos; Shane Barratt; Stephen Boyd; Steven Diamond; J. Zico Kolter
problem: General-purpose differentiation through disciplined convex programs.
method: Disciplined parametrized programming and affine-solver-affine form; analytical differentiation implemented in CVXPY 1.1 with PyTorch/TensorFlow layers (cvxpylayers).
environment_or_data: Applications incl. linear machine learning models (abstract truncated)
key_results: Lowers the barrier to using convex programs in differentiable pipelines (abstract).
limitations: Generic solver-based layer; per-call solve cost (cf. 8.6 ms projection vs 4.5 ms network reported by chen2021enforcing; large overhead in kasaura2023benchmarking).

authors: Mohammed Alshiekh; Roderick Bloem; Ruediger Ehlers; Bettina Koenighofer; S. Niekum; U. Topcu
problem: Learning optimal policies while enforcing safety properties written in temporal logic during learning and execution.
method: Shield: a reactive system synthesised from the temporal-logic specification that monitors the learner's actions and corrects them only when they would violate the specification; conditions under which convergence guarantees are preserved are discussed.
architecture: Shield in the loop of a generic RL learner
environment_or_data: Several RL scenarios (not detailed in abstract)
key_results: Qualitative: specification enforced during learning and execution by construction of the shield.
limitations: Requires a (typically discrete/abstracted) model of safety-relevant dynamics; guarantee holds w.r.t. that abstraction.

authors: Brandon Amos; J. Zico Kolter
problem: Embedding constrained optimisation as a layer of a deep network.
method: OptNet: quadratic programs as layers; exact gradients via sensitivity analysis/implicit differentiation of the KKT conditions; batched GPU primal-dual interior-point solver.
environment_or_data: Synthetic tasks; mini-Sudoku
key_results: Backprop gradients at almost no extra cost on top of the solve; learns hard constraints (mini-Sudoku) (abstract).
limitations: Not an RL paper; layer output is feasible because it is an exact QP solution (up to solver tolerance); per-step cost of an iterative solve.

authors: Muhammad Abdullah Bin Arif; Shahid Iqbal
problem: Electric-bus depot charging on a weak 11 kV feeder with network (voltage) limits and two deadline pools.
method: Two-pool CMDP solved by a 6,165-parameter DQN; network constraint enforced by a closed-form projection applied to the action before the plant; ablation of physics-informed reward vs cost-only reward with/without the layer.
architecture: Small DQN (no ML framework) + closed-form projection
environment_or_data: Measured 11 kV connection, 94-route institutional bus fleet (Gujrat, Pakistan); 40 held-out days
baselines: Uncoordinated charging; perfect-foresight LP bound; reward-shaping ablations
key_results: Daily cost -45.0% vs uncoordinated (340,788 -> 187,335 PKR), 4.4% above LP bound; 0 voltage-floor breaches with projection across seeds/hyperparameters; reward shaping redundant once the layer is present (abstract).
limitations: Abstract only; preprint (no peer review stated); exact projected constraint and any departure-energy guarantee not described in the abstract; no proof stated.

authors: Cheng, B.; Yan, L.; Nan, X.; Sun, B.
problem: Scheduling PV-battery-EV charging station under forecast error
method: One-sided conformal upper bound on net load from forecast residuals, updated online (adaptive conformal), used in rolling-horizon MPC
environment_or_data: PV-storage-charging station case study
key_results: Higher event-period coverage and fewer miscoverage events than fixed conformal; lower low-SOC exposure than point forecast (abstract-level)
limitations: Aggregate net-load bound, not EV departure; abstract only

authors: Cesar Diaz-Londono; Stavros Orfanoudakis; Pedro P. Vergara; Peter Palensky; Fredy Ruiz; Giambattista Gruosso
problem: MPC for G2V/V2G demand response at a charge point operator
method: Economic MPC and optimal-flexibility MPC (LP for G2V, MILP for V2G) integrated with EV2Gym
constraint_handling: other:hard constraints in MPC (departure SoC bound, transformer limit)
environment_or_data: EV2Gym residential scenarios; 10 EVSEs/~25 EVs main case; up to 60 EVSEs for timing
baselines: Charge-as-fast-as-possible; MPC variants against each other
key_results: eMPC V2G profit 50.8 EUR vs AFAP -47.6 EUR (50 runs); per-step time <1.5% of step at 60 EVSEs
limitations: No perfect-information optimum benchmark; assumes known EV schedules; degradation increases with V2G
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.11963 (preprint version, same authors; published EPSR version not read)

authors: Priya L. Donti; David Rolnick; J. Zico Kolter
problem: Fast approximate solution of optimisation problems with hard constraints by neural networks.
method: DC3: completion of partial solutions to satisfy equality constraints and unrolled gradient-based correction for inequality constraints, both differentiable.
environment_or_data: Synthetic optimisation tasks; AC optimal power flow
key_results: Near-optimal objective values while preserving feasibility (abstract).
limitations: Inequality feasibility relies on a finite number of correction steps (not a closed-form projection); not RL.

authors: Ruben Eland; Stavros Orfanoudakis; Pedro P. Vergara
venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science (ECML PKDD 2025 workshops), vol. 2841
problem: V2G smart charging for an EV aggregator in workplace parking lots, operational constraints
method: Safe RL with Constrained Variational Policy Optimization (CVPO)
environment_or_data: Real charging data from Dutch business parking lots (EV2Gym cited in reference list)
baselines: classic RL baselines, rule-based policies, optimal offline benchmark
key_results: Abstract: CVPO reduces constraint violations versus RL baselines and approaches the offline optimum; generalises to unseen scenarios (no numbers in abstract)
limitations: Abstract only; constraint satisfaction is reduced, not guaranteed; full text paywalled

authors: Fernandez-Zapico, D.; Hofman, T.; Salazar, M.
problem: Energy management of EV charging hub with PV and battery
method: Scenario-based stochastic MPC with conformal (EnbPI, MAPIE) prediction intervals around gradient-boosted forecasts of EV load, PV and prices
environment_or_data: Real EV hub data, 280-day closed-loop test (2021)
baselines: Deterministic MPC with point forecast; perfect-forecast MPC
key_results: Coverage at alpha=0.1 about 0.90 for EV load (Tab. II); stochastic MPC 13% costlier than perfect forecast and 1% better than point-forecast MPC
limitations: Conformal used on aggregate load, not per-EV departure; coverage degrades for prices; no RL

authors: Gabriele G.; Pavirani F.; Karimi Madahi S.S.; Develder C.
problem: Single-charger sequential EV charging with unknown departure time (30-min steps, time-varying price)
method: Decision-focused RL (DF-RL): departure-time forecaster trained end-to-end with feedback from the RL charging agent; forecast appended to the state (Sec. 3)
architecture: Actor-critic agent with a learned forecaster; not size-agnostic (one charging point)
environment_or_data: Real sessions from a hospital parking facility (RENergetic project); 20 most frequent users modelled statistically; 350 training / 120 test sessions; fixed 6.5 kW charging power (Sec. 4)
baselines: BAU charge-on-arrival; RL without forecast; RL with MSE-trained forecaster; RL with true departure
key_results: Abstract: up to 14% higher total reward and 55% less unsupplied energy than RL without departure forecasting; conclusion: about 5% reward gain and 14% less unmet energy vs a conventional (MSE) forecaster
limitations: Soft penalty for unmet energy (fixed + quadratic); no coverage or feasibility guarantee; single charger, one price profile; preprint

authors: Shangding Gu; Long Yang; Yali Du; Guang Chen; Florian Walter; Jun Wang; Alois Knoll
venue: IEEE Trans. Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
problem: Survey of safe RL methods, theory and applications.
method: Review organised around five questions ('2H3W'); classifies methods (primal-dual/Lagrangian, trust-region CPO family, formal methods/shielding, Lyapunov, Gaussian-process) and constraint types (cumulative, instantaneous, state-based).
environment_or_data: Benchmarks: AI Safety Gridworlds, Safety Gym, Safe Control Gym, multi-agent safe benchmarks
key_results: Distinguishes cumulative (discounted, mean, probabilistic) from instantaneous constraints (Sec. 2.2); notes that few safety-layer methods offer rigorous guarantees during training.
limitations: Power/energy applications only lightly covered; action-projection layers treated briefly.
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.10330 (arXiv version of the TPAMI article) ; https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/batch (abstract field)

authors: Liangliang Hao; Jiangliang Jin; Yunjian Xu

baselines: Alternative pricing and charging schemes (details not read)

limitations: Abstract only; constraint enforcement details not read

authors: Henderson, P.; Islam, R.; Bachman, P.; Pineau, J.; Precup, D.; Meger, D.
problem: Reproducibility of deep RL
method: Empirical study of seeds, hyperparameters, implementations, reporting; significance testing

limitations: n/a

authors: Joshi, C. K.; Cappart, Q.; Rousseau, L.-M.; Laurent, T.
problem: Zero-shot generalisation of neural TSP solvers to larger instances
method: Controlled study of NCO pipelines (architectures, SL vs RL, decoding)
architecture: GNN / attention encoders with autoregressive or non-autoregressive decoders
environment_or_data: Synthetic TSP instances, train small / test larger
baselines: Classical solvers and recent learned solvers

authors: Kazumi Kasaura; Shuwa Miura; Tadashi Kozuno; Ryo Yonetani; Kenta Hoshino; Y. Hosoe
problem: Benchmarking action-constrained RL (each action must satisfy constraints) in robotics control.
method: Compares closest-point projection with critic on projected (DPro) or pre-projected actions (DPre), differentiable optimisation layer (DOpt via cvxpylayers), Frank-Wolfe (NFWPO), alpha-projection, radial squashing, and penalty variants (Sec. III-IV).
environment_or_data: MuJoCo-type robotics tasks (Reacher, HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker) with box, L2-ball, weighted linear-sum upper bounds, sums of positive parts, quadratic and state-dependent constraints
key_results: Training the critic on pre-projected actions (DPre/SPre, + penalty) is a strong simple baseline; DOpt has large runtime overhead without clear gains; zero-gradient problem of projection explicitly discussed (Sec. III-A, IV-E).
limitations: Robotics only; DOpt limited by cvxpylayers support and run at reduced batch size; four environments.

authors: Kool, W.; van Hoof, H.; Welling, M.
problem: Routing combinatorial optimisation (TSP, VRP variants, OP, PCTSP)
method: REINFORCE with greedy-rollout baseline
architecture: Attention-based encoder-decoder over node tokens (variable number of nodes)
environment_or_data: Synthetic routing instances up to 100 nodes
baselines: Pointer networks, learned heuristics, specialised solvers
key_results: Near-optimal TSP up to 100 nodes; one hyper-parameter set works across several routing problems (abstract-level); abstract does not claim size generalisation
limitations: Abstract makes no zero-shot size-transfer claim

authors: Lee, Z. J.; Li, T.; Low, S. H.
problem: Open workplace EV charging dataset
method: Dataset release and analysis; Gaussian mixture models to learn/predict user behaviour
environment_or_data: ACN-Data (Caltech, JPL; >30,000 sessions at release)
key_results: Shows predicting user behaviour (incl. session parameters) with GMMs; solar sizing and duck-curve smoothing examples (abstract-level)

authors: Zachary J. Lee; George Lee; Ted Lee; Cheng Jin; Rand Lee; Zhi Low; Daniel Chang; Christine Ortega; Steven H. Low
problem: Real-world large-scale workplace smart charging (Caltech ACN) under congested infrastructure
method: Adaptive Scheduling Algorithm: convex optimisation solved in MPC fashion (re-solve on events or every 5 min)
constraint_handling: other:hard infrastructure constraints in convex program + energy as <= constraint with non-completion penalty
environment_or_data: Caltech ACN (54 EVSEs on one transformer, 10,415 sessions May-Oct 2018); ACN-Sim
baselines: Uncontrolled, round robin, LLF, EDF; offline optimal with perfect information
key_results: Profit ~3.4x uncontrolled; 98.1% of offline optimum in idealised setting and ~90% with non-ideal batteries/EVSEs; up to 14.1% more energy than EDF at 30 kW transformer capacity
limitations: Energy delivery best-effort (<=), not guaranteed; requires per-step optimisation; unbalanced three-phase handled via SOC or conservative affine constraints

authors: Tongxin Li; Bo Sun; Yue Chen; Zixin Ye; Steven H. Low; Adam Wierman
problem: Real-time aggregator-operator coordination of EV charging with privacy of load constraints
method: Maximum entropy feedback (MEF) learned with SAC; penalized predictive control (PPC) at operator
architecture: MLP actor-critic (SAC) producing a probability vector over discrete aggregate power levels
constraint_handling: penalty+other:LLF dispatch for per-EV rate/arrival constraints
environment_or_data: Caltech ACN-Data (54 chargers, 150 kW, 12-min slots); CAISO prices
baselines: Vanilla MPC with full state; offline optimal
key_results: Theorem: PPC with exact MEF reproduces offline optimum under strict convexity/log-concavity; learned MEF gives 'almost' feasible results; PPC cost below MPC in plots (no percentage reported)
limitations: Guarantee only for exact MEF and continuous scalar action; learned MEF uses reward penalties; experiments use discrete levels

authors: Lindemann, L.; Cleaveland, M.; Shim, G.; Pappas, G. J.
problem: Planning among dynamic agents with probabilistic safety
method: Trajectory predictor + split conformal prediction regions inside MPC (open- and closed-loop)
environment_or_data: CARLA simulator, pedestrian-filled intersection
key_results: Score = prediction error norm; C = ceil((k+1)(1-delta))-th smallest score; union bound across horizon; probabilistic safety (e.g. >=95% with delta=0.05) confirmed empirically over 100 MPC runs
limitations: Requires exchangeable offline trajectory data; recursive feasibility assumed; union bound conservative

authors: Panagiotis Michailidis; Iakovos Michailidis; Elias Kosmatopoulos
problem: Review of RL for EV charging station control (2015-2025)
method: Structured survey: value-based, policy-based, actor-critic, hybrid
environment_or_data: >200 screened papers; citation thresholds
baselines: Reports common baselines: rule-based/TOU, LP/MILP offline, MPC, greedy
key_results: Departure demand typically a reward penalty; transformer limits stated as physical constraints; gaps: safety, explainability, simulation reliance, no standard EVCS benchmark, multi-agent non-stationarity

authors: Saeed Naghdizadegan Jahromi; Evgenii Genov; Thierry Coosemans; Cedric De Cauwer
problem: EV charging in real-time imbalance market at an office parking facility under price and departure uncertainty
method: Model-free PPO
environment_or_data: 2023 Belgian imbalance prices; office parking
key_results: Policies trained without departure uncertainty outperform those trained with stochastic departures; 1-minute price noise cuts flexibility volume 5% but returns <1%
limitations: Abstract only

authors: Orfanoudakis S.; Oliehoek F.A.; Palensky P.; Vergara P.P.
problem: Network-level EV charging with voltage limits: IEEE 34-bus with 150 V2G chargers; IEEE 123-bus with 500 chargers
method: PI-TD3: TD3 with actor gradients back-propagated through K-step rollouts of a differentiable power-flow and SoC model
architecture: Not specified in preprint; flat state whose length grows with fleet/network size
environment_or_data: EV2Gym + RL-ADN power flow; ElaadNL-based arrivals; 15-min steps, 300-step episodes
baselines: CAFAP, no charging, SAC, PPO, TD3, oracle MPC (perfect information)
key_results: 34-bus: user satisfaction 95.6+-3.6% vs TD3 90.2% and oracle MPC 99.9%; voltage violations per bus 104.2 vs TD3 127.8 and MPC 98.7
limitations: Voltage and departure energy only as soft penalties; no transfer across fleet sizes/topologies; architecture unreported

authors: Javier Sales-Ortiz; Omid Ardakanian
venue: Proc. 15th ACM Int. Conf. Future and Sustainable Energy Systems (e-Energy '24)
problem: VPP trading aggregate bidirectional EV flexibility in a real-time market.
method: Aggregate EV storage so that the RL policy is independent of the number of contracts/EVs; constrain the RL action within bounds that ensure individual charging requirements; proportionally fair disaggregation to chargers.
architecture: Single aggregate RL agent + rule-based disaggregation
environment_or_data: Real-world EV dataset (details not read)
key_results: Robust performance under price uncertainty and shifts in EV mobility distribution (abstract).
limitations: Abstract only (full text blocked); whether feasibility is proven is unknown to us; aggregation hides per-EV heterogeneity in the policy.

authors: Schulman, J.; Moritz, P.; Levine, S.; Jordan, M. I.; Abbeel, P.
problem: Variance reduction in policy gradients
method: Generalized advantage estimation (exponentially weighted TD residuals, analogous to TD(lambda)) + trust-region updates
environment_or_data: 3D locomotion (MuJoCo)
key_results: Strong results on 3D locomotion tasks (abstract-level)
limitations: bib year from arXiv is 2015; ICLR 2016

authors: John Schulman; Filip Wolski; Prafulla Dhariwal; Alec Radford; Oleg Klimov
problem: Simple, sample-efficient on-policy policy-gradient optimisation.
method: Proximal Policy Optimization: clipped surrogate objective allowing multiple epochs of minibatch updates per batch.
environment_or_data: Simulated robotic locomotion, Atari
baselines: Other online policy-gradient methods incl. TRPO (abstract)
key_results: Outperforms other online policy-gradient methods with favourable sample complexity/simplicity trade-off (abstract).
limitations: No constraint handling; constraints must be added (penalty, Lagrangian, or action layer).

authors: Ge Song; Hongbin Xie; Jingyuan Zhang; Hongdi Fu; Zhuoran Shi; Defan Feng; Xuan Song; Haoran Zhang
problem: Long-term energy management of multiple collaborating charging stations
method: MAHEM: transformer-based MARL with attention communication, Q-value decomposition, future-state prediction
architecture: Transformer over temporal sequences; attention-based inter-agent communication
environment_or_data: Not read
key_results: 31.6% reduction in total charging cost vs baselines; robustness and transfer tests claimed
limitations: Abstract only (SSRN page); tokens appear to be time/agents, not chargers; constraint handling unknown

authors: Tong Su; Tong Wu; Junbo Zhao; Anna Scaglione; Le Xie
problem: Review of safe RL methods for power-system operation and control.
method: Taxonomy (Sec. III, Fig. 4): penalised reward; learning-process modification (Lagrangian/primal-dual, Lyapunov, Gaussian process, barrier function, robust RL); RL-structure adjustment (projection/trust region, shielding, safety layer); Table II compares pros/cons.
environment_or_data: Power-system applications: security control, real-time operation, planning, emerging areas
key_results: Classifies projection, Lyapunov, shielding and (strictly applied) safety layers as hard-constraint methods and Lagrangian, barrier, GP as soft/probabilistic (Sec. III-I); scalability of projection/safety layers flagged as a barrier.
limitations: Visible text did not discuss gradients through projection or differentiable optimisation layers; EV subsection truncated in our reading.
evidence_source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.00304 (arXiv version; read up to Sec. IV)

authors: Daniel Tabas; Baosen Zhang
problem: Safe RL for frequency regulation with guaranteed state constraints and no online projection/MPC.
method: Closed-form, differentiable safety filter: gauge map from the l-infinity unit ball onto the state-dependent safe action polytope derived from a robust controlled-invariant (RCI) polytope plus linear backup K x (Sec. III, Eq. 12-13, Thm. 1); trained end-to-end with DDPG.
architecture: DDPG actor (2x256 ReLU, sigmoid output) + gauge-map layer
environment_or_data: Modified 9-bus system with 3 synchronous generators, 3 IBRs, 3 loads (0.05 s steps)
baselines: Robust linear feedback; DDPG with constraint-violation penalties
key_results: Learned policy has lower cost than robust linear feedback with the same safe set; penalty-DDPG leaves the safe set in training and violates constraints at test (Figs. 5-7, no numeric counts).
limitations: Linear dynamics with bounded disturbances; RCI set computed offline by SDP; single small test system; no timing comparison.

authors: Chen Tessler; Daniel J. Mankowitz; Shie Mannor
problem: Constrained RL where reward misspecification is avoided by explicit constraints.
method: Reward Constrained Policy Optimization (RCPO): multi-timescale Lagrangian approach in which a learned penalty signal (multiplier) steers the policy toward constraint satisfaction.
environment_or_data: not read (abstract only)
key_results: Qualitative: convergence of the multi-timescale scheme is proved; empirical evidence of constraint-satisfying policies.
limitations: Convergence is asymptotic and the constraint is on (discounted/average) cost; violations can occur during training.

authors: Tuchnitz, F.; Ebell, N.; Schlund, J.; Pruckner, M.
problem: Smart charging coordination of an EV fleet considering grid baseload
method: Deep RL (value-based with prioritised experience variants)
architecture: Central agent with neural network function approximator producing schedules for a fleet of any size (abstract)
environment_or_data: Case study with baseload profile
baselines: Uncontrolled charging; optimisation-based strategy with perfect information; other strategies
key_results: Load variance reduced by 65% vs uncontrolled; all EVs reported sufficiently charged at departure; close to optimisation benchmark (abstract-level)
limitations: Abstract does not report training vs test fleet sizes; constraint satisfaction empirical

authors: Vaswani, A.; Shazeer, N.; Parmar, N.; Uszkoreit, J.; Jones, L.; Gomez, A. N.; Kaiser, L.; Polosukhin, I.

authors: Wan G.; Zeng P.; Dong X.; Song C.; Cui S.; Li D.; et al.
problem: Hybrid-action CPS optimisation incl. an EV charging station scenario (transformer capacity, charger current limits)

environment_or_data: Custom simulations (not EV2Gym)
key_results: EV station: zero transformer/current violations vs 24.77% (PDQN) and 57.34% (HPPO); 90.4% per-vehicle success

authors: Bo Wang; Lanyu Lin; Yong-Jin Liu
problem: Euclidean projection onto the intersection of a half-space and a box-like set, and its generalised Jacobian.
method: Lagrangian duality reduces the projection to a univariate semismooth equation solved by a semismooth Newton method with line-search safeguard; explicit generalised Jacobian of the projection derived.
environment_or_data: Very large-scale projection problems
key_results: Global and locally quadratic convergence; outperforms standard solvers (abstract).
limitations: Abstract only; half-space (inequality) version - equality-sum case is the hyperplane special case.

authors: Wang, M.; Feng, M.; Zhou, W.; Li, H.
problem: Active voltage control in distribution networks with PV inverters
method: T-MAAC with MADDPG/MATD3
architecture: Transformer policy with bus tokens, adjacency-masked attention, agent-centric readout; parameters shared across agents with agent ID; transformer critic over agents
environment_or_data: MAPDN 141-bus (22 agents) and 322-bus (38 agents)
key_results: Controllable rate e.g. 141-bus spring 75.8%->97.8% (MADDPG), 322-bus spring 59.4%->90.6% (MATD3) (Table 1); each network trained separately, no cross-size transfer
limitations: Per-network training; soft barrier penalties; CR below 100%

authors: Xiong, R.; Yang, Y.; He, D.; Zheng, K.; Zheng, S.; Xing, C.; Zhang, H.; Lan, Y.; Wang, L.; Liu, T.-Y.

key_results: Post-LN has large expected gradients near the output at init, needing warm-up; Pre-LN gradients well-behaved, warm-up can be removed with comparable results and faster training
limitations: Analysis at initialisation

authors: Yunus Emre Yılmaz; Stavros Orfanoudakis; Pedro P. Vergara

key_results: Theorem characterising permutation-invariant set functions; architecture applies to sets of any cardinality (abstract-level)
limitations: Not RL; sum pooling has limited interaction modelling between elements

problem: Real-time charging power control of a dynamic number of EVs in distribution network (voltage, bill, comfort)

key_results: Mitigates voltage fluctuation, reduces bill, improves battery comfort (qualitative per abstract)
limitations: Variable-N handled by grouping (state aggregation) rather than per-EV tokens; abstract only

limitations: Abstract only; PCPO projects policy parameters (expected-cost constraint), not per-step actions

method: Decentralised DDPG per charging unit with energy-boundary model and relaxation; smart-charging choice model from survey

limitations: Abstract only

limitations: arXiv only

authors: Caballe, J.; Segovia, P.; Ocampo-Martinez, C.; Quijano, N.
problem: Large-scale EV charging coordination with nodal capacity limits and battery degradation

key_results: Mean-field-type games minimise unmet energy and queueing; DRL highest average final SOC (~81%) under volatile tariffs (abstract-level); mean-field policies epsilon-Nash as fleet grows

authors: Glenn Ceusters; Muhammad Andy Putratama; Ruediger Franke; Ann Nowe; M. Messagie
problem: Safe RL with hard constraints for multi-energy management systems where constraint functions are imperfectly known.
method: OptLayerPolicy: QP projection (OptLayer) of the proposed action onto the constraint set, switching to a hand-designed SafeFallback policy if the projection distance exceeds a threshold; self-improving constraints via learned MLP residuals (Sec. 3, Alg. 1-2).
architecture: TD3 (Stable-Baselines) + external QP safety layer (projected action sent to environment, no gradient through the QP)
environment_or_data: Simulated multi-energy system: grid, 0.8 MWe wind, 1.0 MWe PV, gas boiler, heat pump, CHP, 3.5 MWh TESS, 2.0 MWh BESS
key_results: Initial utility 92.4% (OptLayerPolicy) vs 86.1% (OptLayer); constraint-tolerance NSUM 6.1-6.5% for safety layers vs 22.3% for unsafe TD3 (Tables 3-4); about 1.9 s per step for the grey-box variant.
limitations: No formal proof; residual model mismatch; per-step solve cost; single simulated case; only TD3 tested.

authors: Christensen K.; Jorgensen B.N.; Ma Z.G.
problem: Residential LV feeder (Strib, Denmark), 126 households all with EVs under a 400 kVA transformer; one-year minute-resolution simulation
method: Rule-based aggregator: shifts highest-laxity EVs out of overload hours to cheapest feasible slots (no learning)

key_results: Abstract: overloads completely eliminated; aggregator compensation under DKK 6000/year, far below transformer reinforcement cost

authors: Demirel G.; Grafenhorst S.; Ohm J.; Schafer B.; Forderer K.; Hagenmeyer V.

authors: Jiarong Fan; Ariel Liebman; Hao Wang
problem: EV charging-station management in a distribution network under voltage constraints and solar/price uncertainty.

key_results: Cost 926 vs 933 (SAC) and 1091 (DDPG) $; voltage-violation count 294 vs 436 and 551; unfinished demand 411.2 kWh (Table I).

architecture: Transformer tokens are time steps of one station's observation window, not chargers; one agent per station
environment_or_data: IEEE 33-bus PDN, 4 stations x 10 chargers, 5-min steps; Caltech ACN EV data, Ausgrid PV, AEMO prices (Sec. IV-A)

key_results: About 45% fewer voltage violations and about 10% lower cost than MARL baselines (abstract)
limitations: Voltage and demand satisfaction only via Lagrangian regularisation; scalability discussed qualitatively (App. B2), not tested; fixed number of stations
